scoreRule: 1 point per correct MC item; 10 points maximum; local provisional grade only
description: Original independent letter comprehension C2 draft, not approved.

questions.q: What makes Elias's account of his busy life 'conveniently incomplete'?
choices: It invents jobs in cities where he has never lived.
It incorrectly suggests that travel consumes time.
It assumes that writing letters is always quicker than posting.
It offers plausible circumstances while omitting his active preference for curated updates.
questions.explanation: He acknowledges that his explanation is not false but conceals choices he made.

questions.q: What distinction underlies the question about information and the availability of a person?
choices: Frequent online updates eliminate the need for friendship.
Knowing someone's public whereabouts does not ensure access to their private experience.
All written information is less accurate than spoken conversation.
Location information is inherently dishonest.
questions.explanation: Elias realises he can tell acquaintances where he is but not tell Amara why he is lost.

questions.q: What is ethically important about retaining the dockworker's contradictory memories?
choices: It refuses to turn lived complexity into a falsely reassuring communal narrative.
It demonstrates that solidarity cannot exist in a difficult neighbourhood.
It establishes that the dockworker's account is the only valid history.
It makes the exhibition intentionally confusing.
questions.explanation: The account allows solidarity and resentment to coexist without a tidy ending.

questions.q: Why might listening require abandoning the pleasure of being useful?
choices: Interviewers should never offer practical assistance.
A museum cannot include stories with unresolved problems.
Premature solutions can overwrite a person's complicated experience.
Every difficult experience should be kept private.
questions.explanation: Elias reflects on offering tidy solutions rather than attending to Amara's complexity.

questions.q: Why are the fisherman's brief postcards valuable without cancelling his long absence?
choices: Their factual details prove that he was always a good father.
The family treats them as proof he never travelled.
They explain why he stopped communicating in person.
They offer limited but genuine signs of attention without pretending to repair everything.
questions.explanation: The daughter values honest fragments while refusing to romanticise her absent father.

questions.q: What contrast does Elias draw between the postcards and his own polished updates?
choices: His updates were written on paper and the postcards online.
The postcards acknowledge their modest scope rather than displaying artificial completeness.
The postcards gave elaborate accounts of every difficult emotion.
His updates were too short to reach an audience.
questions.explanation: The postcard messages never claim to be more than a sign of life.

questions.q: What makes the timing of Elias's letter ethically uncomfortable?
choices: His museum project has ended before the letter is written.
Amara has already agreed to attend the event.
His wish for Amara's company at an upcoming museum event may colour his renewed concern.
Elias has promised to pay for everyone's travel.
questions.explanation: He recognises the suspicion that he remembered the friendship only when he wanted an audience.

questions.q: Why would asking Amara to reassure him about his sincerity worsen matters?
choices: It would make her responsible for managing his guilt rather than freely responding.
It would prevent Elias from explaining the museum's work.
It would require the museum to cancel the event.
It would reveal private information about another interviewee.
questions.explanation: Elias explicitly rejects transferring emotional labour to Amara.

questions.q: What is the value of proposing letters without an expectation of immediate replies?
choices: It ensures that neither person will ever feel disappointed.
It gives both changed people room to reconnect without demanding an earlier closeness.
It allows Elias to avoid reading Amara's replies.
It guarantees they will restore their friendship exactly as before.
questions.explanation: The final paragraph wants contact without requiring either to become a reassuring memory.

questions.q: What does Elias mean by refusing to treat Amara's response as a verdict on his worth?
choices: He no longer considers friendship valuable.
He believes every refusal would prove the letter succeeded.
He expects her to justify any decision in detail.
He intends to respect her independent choice instead of using it to judge himself.
questions.explanation: The letter rejects turning an invitation into a moral test of either person.
